A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 22-page versions of Jailbreaking as a Reward Misspecification Problem, including Appendices A–D. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original ReGap backdoor-detection experiments and ReMiss evaluations, including attack success, transferability, readability, and ablation results in Sections 3.2 and 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results from v3, including the backdoor-detection analysis, benchmark evaluations, transfer experiments, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The ReGap objective, ReMiss training and inference procedures, and stochastic beam search remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions retain AdvBench, HarmBench, and the backdoor-detection evaluation described in Appendix D. The evaluated transfer, system-prompt, and defense scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: AdvPrompter, AutoDAN, and GCG retain the same participation in the corresponding comparisons. Zhou et al. (2024) is added only as a related-work citation, not as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C retain the same data splits, evaluation metrics, model configurations, decoding procedures, and training settings. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The perplexity and suffix-length analyses, system-prompt and safeguard tests, evaluator comparisons, reference-model ablation, ROC analysis, and appendix case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix C.6 states that performance is reported from a single training run in both versions. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains ReMiss's 98.1% test ASR@10 on Vicuna-7b-v1.5.

T1.justification: The implicit-reward derivation in Section 2.1, reward-misspecification definition and ReGap formula in Section 3.1, and mathematical discussion in Appendix B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same reward-misspecification framing and claims about ReGap, ReMiss, attack effectiveness, readability, and transferability.

C2.justification: Interpretations of ReGap, reference-model regularization, model susceptibility, and discovered attack modes remain unchanged. The access assumptions and qualifications in Section 4.2 and Appendix B are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, model identifiers, and evaluation instructions are identical. The code and resource links also retain the same destinations.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Zhou et al. (2024), Don't say no: Jailbreaking LLM by suppressing refusal, to the existing discussion of difficulties caused by high initial-token loss. Its bibliography entry is added on page 14; the surrounding research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The corresponding-author footnote marker is corrected from 2 to a dagger, matching the author-line markers, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Apart from the added citation, the prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The citation addition causes local paragraph and bibliography reflow, and footnote formatting shifts slightly. Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–14 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: The additional supporting citation and corrected corresponding-author marker provide small editorial benefits. However, the arguments, methods, empirical evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout both PDFs, so the revision does not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
